title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.32854v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is now a standard approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks. Its low-rank factorization is inherently non-identifiable, making LoRA a singular statistical model whose learning complexity cannot be described by parameter dimension alone. We study this complexity using the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from singular learning theory and how it depends on both the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network. Under a local linearization, LoRA induces a low-rank trace regression model whose Kullback--Leibler geometry is controlled by a forward-backward covariance, constructed from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. This covariance determines which low-rank perturbations are statistically observable. tldr: 本文借助奇异学习理论中的实对数典型阈值（RLCT）刻画了LoRA作为奇异统计模型的学习复杂度，证明该复杂度由适应层前向激活与反向传播敏感度构成的协方差决定，并在非退化情形下恢复降秩回归的经典复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper characterizes the learning complexity of LoRA as a singular statistical model via the real log canonical threshold (RLCT), showing that it is governed by a forward-backward covariance built from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer, recovering the classical complexity of reduced-rank regression in the nondegenerate case.
